summary: ```markdown # Modular Configurator & Autofitting Toolset Tutorial Welcome to the tutorial on the Modular Configurator and Autofitting tools. In this guide, we will walk through the features and functionalities of these tools, enabling efficient garment design and fitting. ## Overview of the Modular Configurator The Modular Configurator can be found under the window drop-down menus. There are three basic groups: women's, men's, and folded shirts. ### Women's Clothing Options Selecting the women's category, you will find many block types ranging from jackets to trench coats. Under shirts, you will see options for long sleeves. There are many choices in these blocks for different modular styles, but all maintain the same base fit. ### Adding Assets to the Scene To incorporate assets into your design, click them to bring them into the scene. For demonstration, let's add these to a default avatar: 1. Select the avatar folder. 2. Choose a female avatar to bring her into the scene. 3. Go to the pose folder and change her pose to the "attention pose." This is the pose the modular mode assets are made with. Select "pose only" and then click "OK." ## Working with Modular Blocks Once the avatar is in place, bring up the Modular Configurator window again. Select women's blocks and then choose t-shirts. In this example, I will select the rounded neck and short sleeves. ### Simulating Garment Fit Turn on simulation to have the garment settle into place. The pattern pieces are organized in modular frames, allowing you to replace pieces with others if necessary. To remove these frames, right-click the 2D window and select "Remove Modular Relationship." After that, you can now use more modular assets if you want. ## Introduction to Autofitting Tools Next, we will explore the autofitting tools. To use these tools effectively for both the model and the garment: 1. Select the avatar and the garment that need a fitting suit. 2. Check in the 3D window for avatar and garment display options, ensuring they have a black and red one respectively. ### Preparing for Autofitting As long as both the target avatar and the donor garment have fitting suits, you can utilize the tools. Make sure the garment's particle distance is set to 20. Then, select the autofitting tool in the 2D window and keep curvature at 100%. Once done, select "OK." This performs two actions: auto-fitting and auto-target redraping. After completion, the garment is resized onto the target avatar. ## Retarget Draping Tool Apart from auto-fitting, there is another tool called "retarget draping." This tool allows you to place a garment onto an avatar without changing its size. ### Example of Retarget Draping For example, we will take a men's sweatshirt and place it onto Hannah for an oversized look. Ensure the particle distance is set to 20 for speed, and verify they both fit and have fitting suits via the 3D display options. Then select "retarget draping," and the sweatshirt will be placed on Hannah. To ensure proper placement, I will turn off the hair so it sits correctly. ## Adding Fitting Suits to Custom Avatars Next, let’s discuss how to add fitting suits to your custom avatars. Fitting suits are designed for two-armed, two-legged, and one-headed avatars and are not intended for use with avatars that have additional limbs. ### Importing Custom Avatars To add a fitting suit to your custom avatars, go to **File** > **Import**, and select either FBX or OBJ file types. Choose your file, importing it as an avatar, and ensure to turn on "Auto-Create Fitting Suit." ### Checking the Fitting Suit Quality If your file scale is correct, it should load successfully. Toggle on the "View Avatar Fitting Suit" option to check the quality of the auto-created fitting suit. If it looks good, you can start using the tools without making edits. ## Manually Creating a Fitting Suit If you need to manually fix or create a fitting suit, import as normal, but toggle off the "Auto-Create Fitting Suit" option. 1. To add a fitting suit, go to the "Create Fitting Suit" tool and select it. A tool pop-up window will appear. 2. Follow the instructions provided and make sure to select the highlighted limb (most often on the screen left). 3. To create a reference line, click three times to create rings on the avatar in the corresponding locations as listed. Try to keep these as parallel to the ground as possible or aligned with the true joints on the avatar. ### Completing the Fitting Suit These lines will determine your fit in the future. If you make a mistake, reselect the option (for example, select the knee again) and remake the ring. Continue this process until the reference lines are completed. Select "Apply" to place the fitting suit on the avatar. Adjust as needed with the left mouse button if there are any intersections with the avatar mesh. Select "Save" when ready. The saved avatar remains in the scene, and you can now use the autofitting tools. ## Final Steps To conclude, bring in pants and check for a garment fitting suit. You can use any avatar with a fitting suit with any garment that also has a garment fitting suit. Select "OK," and we are done. Thank you for watching. The avatar's fitting suit information will be retained, so make sure to save as a new file. ```
